As Holy Week leads to Easter, as Passover begins, and as America approaches its 250th year of independence, this is a season to remember the values that helped shape our nation: faith, freedom, sacrifice, memory, and the importance of religious liberty.
It is also a time to remember something else that too often gets ignored: the American story was built by many hands, including a very small Jewish community in the colonies whose contribution to the nation's founding was vastly disproportionate to its size.
_That matters to me personally._
I have been involved in helping support and raise awareness for _[Washington's Ring of Spies](https://substack.com/redirect/c5e39a2e-d411-4228-b119-bf60cdfe895f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_, a unique production that tells an important and too often overlooked part of the American founding story.
[The Story](https://substack.com/redirect/fb58b275-98d0-4743-a34b-82b27d7d231b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
At the time of the American Revolution, the Jewish population in the colonies was tiny, yet Jews played an outsized role in the life of the Revolution and the building of the republic. _**In a moment like this, when there is an increasing push to erase the Judeo influence from the moral and historical fabric of America, that story is worth telling plainly.**_
That is why this production matters to me. It is not a Jewish production, but it is an honest American one. It tells the broader story of the Revolution and gives proper recognition where it belongs, including to the small Jewish community whose role in the founding far exceeded its numbers. America was never about one person. It was about a team. A people. A fabric woven together by faith, sacrifice, courage, and common purpose into something unique in human history.
### And it is worth telling now.
_**Passover is about deliverance from bondage. Easter comes through Holy Week, with its themes of sacrifice, suffering, redemption, and hope. Christians remember that the Last Supper took place in the setting of Passover. Jews remember that freedom came at a price and had to be marked, remembered, and handed down. In both traditions, memory is not ornamental. It is essential to our survival.**_
That is why America's 250th anniversary should mean more than slogans, branding, and fireworks.
A nation turning 250 should ask harder questions. Do we still know who we are? Do we still understand the principles that gave us birth? Do we still remember the sacrifices of those who carried the cause of liberty when the future of this country was uncertain?
Too often, the answer seems to be no.
_**One of the more troubling developments in our culture is the effort to separate America from the moral inheritance that shaped it. Part of that takes the form of trying to strip the "Judeo" out of "Judeo-Christian." Another part takes the form of minimizing or erasing the Jewish contribution to the founding altogether. But Jews were not guests in America's founding. They were among its builders. As the materials for this production make clear, Jews in colonial America served as financiers, intelligence operatives, merchants, translators, and patriots.**_
[That is why this production matters.](https://substack.com/redirect/fb58b275-98d0-4743-a34b-82b27d7d231b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### The Culper Spy Ring
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0af1b4de-5637-4953-8f66-cf81be0dfa01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The American Revolution was not won only by the famous names everyone learns in school. It was also sustained by hidden networks, private sacrifice, quiet courage, and ordinary people willing to risk everything without any promise of recognition. The Culper Ring is part of that story. _**So is Haym Salomon.**_
Salomon stands as one of the great underappreciated figures of the founding era. At a moment when the Revolution was under enormous strain, he helped sustain the American cause. More broadly, he represents something larger: a small Jewish community that contributed far beyond its numbers to the birth of the republic. That is not a side note. That is American history.
And it ties directly to one of the greatest achievements of the founding: _**Religious Freedom**_.
George Washington understood that clearly. [In his famous letter to the Hebrew Congregation in Newport](https://open.substack.com/pub/drmichaelgoldstein4ct/p/hanukkah-and-our-founding-fathers?utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=post%20viewer), he wrote that the Government of the United States gives _**" to bigotry no sanction, to persecution no assistance**_." Those are not the words of a government offering grudging tolerance. They are the words of a republic recognizing equal citizenship and liberty of conscience as matters of principle.
That distinction matters, especially now.
_**At a time when some revisionist Christians drift into supersessionism, replacement theology, or the removal of "Judeo" from "Judeo-Christian," Washington's words remain a needed corrective. America did not establish itself by pushing Jews to the margins. It recognized them as part of the civic body and entitled to the blessings of liberty. That vision is one of the best parts of the American experiment, and it is worth defending.**_
That is one reason a project like _[Washington's Ring of Spies](https://substack.com/redirect/c5e39a2e-d411-4228-b119-bf60cdfe895f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/c5e39a2e-d411-4228-b119-bf60cdfe895f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)deserves attention.
Culture matters because it can restore memory in ways arguments alone often cannot. A good production can do something a speech or essay cannot. It can put forgotten people back into the story. It can make sacrifice visible again. It can remind families, churches, schools, and communities that the American founding was not built only by public figures in portraits, but also by hidden patriots, immigrant builders, intelligence operatives, and people of faith who gave everything they had for a cause greater than themselves.
This production is part of that effort. It is not just a show. It is an act of remembrance. The materials describe it not simply as a performance, but as part of a broader effort to ensure this history rises louder in a time of antisemitism and erasure. They also describe ambitions beyond the initial production, including touring, filmed performances, educational use, licensing, and materials for future generations.
[And that is why it is especially disappointing when places like Connecticut reject what could be a once-in-a-generation opportunity for some children to participate in meaningful America 250 experiences earlier this year.](https://open.substack.com/pub/drmichaelgoldstein4ct/p/american-independence-cancelled-in?utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=post%20viewer)
This should be the moment when communities lean in, not pull back. We should want young people to encounter the real story of the founding, including its religious dimension, all patriots (including those who were Jewish), its hidden courage, and its moral seriousness. We should want them to understand that liberty requires memory, and that religious freedom is not an afterthought but one of the great pillars of the American experiment.
A healthy country would teach that.
A healthy country would remember that Jews helped build this nation. A healthy country would understand that the Judeo-Christian moral framework is not an embarrassment to be erased, but part of the inheritance that shaped America's understanding of law, dignity, responsibility, and freedom under God.
So yes, if you happen to be in Branson, Missouri later this year, _[Washington's Ring of Spies](https://substack.com/redirect/c5e39a2e-d411-4228-b119-bf60cdfe895f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/c5e39a2e-d411-4228-b119-bf60cdfe895f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)is worth a look.
### _**But the larger point is not about one show in one city. The larger point is whether America, at 250, still has enough honesty left to remember its own builders.**_
As Passover begins and Holy Week leads to Easter, that is exactly the kind of reflection this country should be having.
Wishing you all a Happy Easter and Chag Sameach. It is times like this when we must come together, not by erasing our history, but by remembering it honestly, honoring those who came before us, and carrying that inheritance forward with gratitude.
_**Those who fail to learn from history are condemned to repeat it.**_

Dear Peter, I want to thank you for the trust you've placed in our movement over the years. name: Fran Hong
subject: 100 jobs lost in Fond du Lac
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
Wisconsin workers deserve better
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260401-2677)
Peter,
On Monday, Wells Vehicle Electronics filed a notice with the state of Wisconsin to permanently shut down two facilities in Fond du Lac. One hundred workers — assemblers, technicians, warehouse staff, some of them union members — will lose their jobs.
Wells has been in Fond du Lac since 1903. They got their start making ignition coils for the Ford Model T — the car that put America on wheels. That's over a century of workers making things in Wisconsin. And now a $9 billion multinational parent company that just posted record sales is shutting it down. This isn't a company that couldn't afford to stay. It's a company that decided Wisconsin workers weren't worth keeping.
And here's what makes it worse: In 2012, Wisconsin taxpayers helped pay to expand the very facility that's closing now — a forgivable loan from the county, a TIF district from the city, and over a million dollars in state tax credits. They took the investment and they're walking away.
That's the deal workers keep getting. Corporations take the tax breaks, take the labor, take generations of loyalty from a community — and when the spreadsheet changes, they close the plant and move on. The workers are the last to know and the first to pay.
That's why I co-authored the Economic Justice Bill of Rights. And as governor, I'll fight for working people.
No company should be able to take public dollars and then lay off the workers who made them profitable. If you benefit from Wisconsin taxpayers, you owe something to Wisconsin workers. That's not radical — it's the basic deal, and we're going to put it in writing.
We're going to protect the right to organize — because when workers have a union, they have a seat at the table before the decision gets made, not after the notice gets filed. Wisconsin's unionization rate has been cut in half since 2011. That wasn't an accident. It was a political choice, and we're going to reverse it.
And we're going to guarantee paid leave — because when you lose your job, you shouldn't also lose the ability to take care of your family while you figure out what's next.
The Economic Justice Bill of Rights is built for the people in Fond du Lac and every community where this story keeps playing out. As governor, I’ll hold corporations accountable.
But we're building this movement without PAC money — which means we need you.
[**Every dollar is an investment in building a better Wisconsin.**](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260331.jiZWXk&refcode=em20260401-2677&t=1&akid=2677%2E105371%2EzT-2l8)

Fran

clean_body: Wisconsin workers deserve better Peter, On Monday, Wells Vehicle Electronics filed a notice with the state of Wisconsin to permanently shut down two facilities in Fond du Lac. One hundred workers — assemblers, technicians, warehouse staff, some of them union members — will lose their jobs. Wells has been in Fond du Lac since 1903. They got their start making ignition coils for the Ford Model T — the car that put America on wheels. That's over a century of workers making things in Wisconsin. And now a $9 billion multinational parent company that just posted record sales is shutting it down. This isn't a company that couldn't afford to stay. It's a company that decided Wisconsin workers weren't worth keeping. And here's what makes it worse: In 2012, Wisconsin taxpayers helped pay to expand the very facility that's closing now — a forgivable loan from the county, a TIF district from the city, and over a million dollars in state tax credits. They took the investment and they're walking away. That's the deal workers keep getting. Corporations take the tax breaks, take the labor, take generations of loyalty from a community — and when the spreadsheet changes, they close the plant and move on. The workers are the last to know and the first to pay. That's why I co-authored the Economic Justice Bill of Rights. And as governor, I'll fight for working people. No company should be able to take public dollars and then lay off the workers who made them profitable. If you benefit from Wisconsin taxpayers, you owe something to Wisconsin workers. That's not radical — it's the basic deal, and we're going to put it in writing. We're going to protect the right to organize — because when workers have a union, they have a seat at the table before the decision gets made, not after the notice gets filed. Wisconsin's unionization rate has been cut in half since 2011. That wasn't an accident. It was a political choice, and we're going to reverse it. And we're going to guarantee paid leave — because when you lose your job, you shouldn't also lose the ability to take care of your family while you figure out what's next. The Economic Justice Bill of Rights is built for the people in Fond du Lac and every community where this story keeps playing out. As governor, I’ll hold corporations accountable. But we're building this movement without PAC money — which means we need you. In solidarity, Fran Email us: mailto:info@francescahong.com

Peter, **Something truly unbelievable happened today.** **Donald Trump himself showed up at the Supreme Court for oral arguments on birthright citizenship.** He didn't send a staffer. He didn't get updates at the White House. He sat in the public section, staring down the justices he appointed. No sitting president has EVER done this. Now, they are weighing whether to rip apart the Fourteenth Amendment itself. **The Supreme Court rules with Trump 90% of the time—and his personal intimidation only makes it more likely the justices will strip away birthright citizenship.** [**This democracy belongs to us, not the wannabe dictator. clean_body: Wow. Trump showed up at the Supreme Court’s oral arguments today to intimidate the justices he appointed. | | Peter, Something truly unbelievable happened today. Donald Trump himself showed up at the Supreme Court for oral arguments on birthright citizenship. He didn't send a staffer. He didn't get updates at the White House. He sat in the public section, staring down the justices he appointed. No sitting president has EVER done this. Why? The Supreme Court today heard a case today challenging his Executive Order redefining who gets to be an American. He wants to strip birthright citizenship from thousands of children—and he wants to make sure the Supreme Court gives him the green light to do it. In an unprecedented move, the wannabe mob boss made his presence felt in the courtroom, turning a legal proceeding into a theater of power. This is not what a democracy looks like. Just yesterday, the bought-and-paid-for Supreme Court slashed trans rights, gutting protections for vulnerable communities. Now, they are weighing whether to rip apart the Fourteenth Amendment itself. The Supreme Court rules with Trump 90% of the time—and his personal intimidation only makes it more likely the justices will strip away birthright citizenship. Trump is leading a coordinated effort by the wealthy and powerful to entrench MAGA power for decades to come. They are pulling the strings behind the scenes, and tipping the scales so that ordinary families lose their voice.This is what authoritarianism looks like—a leader showing up to lean on the judges he wants to keep in his pocket. If he succeeds, he’ll have stolen the power to decide who counts as an American, and who doesn’t. That's why United for Democracy is building the mass movement to hold the Court accountable. Our allies, activists, experts, and organizations are mobilizing across the country to make sure the justices know who they really work for. body:
| |
Peter,

Yesterday, the Supreme Court issued a horrific ruling that dismantles protections for LGBTQ young people, including laws that ban conversion therapy.

**Before I go on, it’s important that America’s LGBTQ youth hear this clearly: You are not broken. You do not need to be fixed. There is nothing wrong with who you are. Conversion therapy is a lie. It doesn’t work. And it causes real, lasting harm. If you’re struggling right now, please know this: you are loved. You are seen. You matter. I will never stop fighting for you. 🏳️⚧️🌈**

Every major medical organization has condemned conversion therapy as dangerous, ineffective, and deeply harmful. That’s why California, 23 other states, and Washington, D.C. have banned it.

I’ve taken action here in California to expand survivors’ ability to hold the people who harmed them accountable. But clearly, this fight doesn’t end at our state line.

These attacks are national, and they’re picking up momentum as shameless bigots try to erase LGBTQ people and drag us backwards.

**[Today, I’m asking you to stand with me and with LGBTQ people across the country as we demand justice and action.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128600530/611743448/-262479427?refcode=SW_EM_PT_180DO_260401_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDY5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3ZDhlZDliMy0xZjJlLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lutbX-bEFVlYJGfrO3K5-O9XuLHKB9knkK0RNRgcRMI=&emci=b55a6c56-1f2e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=7d8ed9b3-1f2e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=53530144)**

---

We will not let extremists or courts use LGBTQ youth as their political punching bag. Period.

Yesterday was also the first debate of our race, and it reminded me of a simple fact: San Francisco has never been represented by an LGBTQ person in Congress.

If I’m elected, that changes. And it matters, because representation isn’t about checking a box. It’s about having someone in the room, every day, ready to push back when extremists try to erase our community, target our kids, and roll back our rights.

This campaign is about making sure our voices are heard where it matters most. _[**Please add your name today to stand with LGBTQ Americans against conversion therapy.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128600548/611743473/-262479427?refcode=SW_EM_PT_180DO_260401_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDY5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3ZDhlZDliMy0xZjJlLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lutbX-bEFVlYJGfrO3K5-O9XuLHKB9knkK0RNRgcRMI=&emci=b55a6c56-1f2e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=7d8ed9b3-1f2e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=53530144)_

Fellow Conservative: The Senate is a big problem. The Democrats want to destroy our country, and far too many Republicans are unwilling to do anything about it. That's why we must unite to support strong Senate candidates in the midterm elections. Not the candidates hand-picked by the Washington machine. We need fighters — proven by their records, battle-tested, and ready to take on the establishment. The Senate Conservatives Fund has endorsed a strong group of them, and we need your help to get them across the finish line. Here's who's in the fight:
---
|
---
---
# Nate Morris

---
# U.S. Senate | Kentucky

---
# May 19 (Primary)

---

Boebert has taken millions from corporate PACs, extremist donors, and even Elon Musk. But not us. We’re funding our campaign just $22 at a time – entirely from grassroots donors like you. Which is why it was so important as we faced our first FEC deadline of the year last night that we hit our fundraising goal. And with your help, we did just that. Thank you. I truly could not be doing any of this without you. Every day as I crisscross Colorado’s 4th congressional district, I meet Democrats, Republicans, and independents who are absolutely fed up with Lauren Boebert. There’s a reason she only won by 546 votes against Adam Frisch. We’re heading into the next phase of this race, and it’s critical we not let up for even one day if we’re going to finally send Lauren Boebert packing this November. I’m all-in, and knowing that you have my back fuels me to work even harder. Together, we are going to win and finally put an end to Lauren Boebert embarrassing political career. Thank you – for everything.
